artificial systems to autonomously formulate meaningful objectives is a cornerstone of true artificial general intelligence. Traditional AI architectures rely on human‑supplied goals, creating a fixed mapping from human intent to system action. In contrast, the Computational Goal Generation Theory (CGGT) proposes a formal framework by which a system can internally generate, evaluate, and refine its own goals, thereby becoming a self‑directed agent. CGGT integrates principles from decision theory, reinforcement learning, and cognitive science to model the process of goal discovery as a dynamic optimization problem over the space of possible goal functions. This paper presents the core mathematical formulation of CGGT, elaborates on the mechanisms for goal proposal, validation, and selection, and discusses how the theory can be embedded into existing AI architectures.
